formation.title: The Birth of Finland
formation.text:
The Finnish lands have been united under a single banner for the first time. For centuries, these territories at the edge of the known world served as a frontier between East and West: a land of endless forests, countless lakes, and a people hardened by the harshest winters in Europe. Now the question falls to us: what shall Finland become? Shall we embrace the character of our land: the impenetrable wilderness, the frozen lakes that swallow armies, the sisu that lets our people endure what others cannot? Or shall we look outward to the trade routes that connect us to the wider world: the tar that every navy needs, the furs that every court desires, the timber that builds the ships of nations?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the land itself. Let invaders break upon our forests.

modifiers.name: Land of a Thousand Lakes
modifiers.text: Finland's identity is forged in its vast wilderness, dense forests, frozen lakes, and unyielding terrain that has shaped a people of extraordinary resilience. The Finnish frontier is a shield against any invader, where every forest trail becomes an ambush and every frozen lake a barrier.

options.text: Our wealth flows through our rivers and forests to the world.

modifiers.name: Northern Trade Ways
modifiers.text: From the tar kilns of Ostrobothnia to the fur markets of the interior, Finland's wealth flows through its forests and waterways. Finnish tar seals the hulls of Europe's navies, Finnish furs warm the courts of the continent, and Finnish timber builds the cities of the Baltic.

advances.name: Rajakartano
advances.text: Fortified border manors serving as military outposts and administrative centers along the Finnish frontier, their garrisons providing the first line of defense against eastern raiders.

advances.name: Border Soldiers
advances.text: The eastern frontier bred a distinctive warrior tradition. Finnish border soldiers learned to fight in dense forests and frozen terrain, developing defensive tactics that exploited the landscape against numerically superior foes.

advances.name: Kaskiviljely
advances.text: The Finnish technique of slash-and-burn agriculture transformed dense pine and spruce forests into fertile cropland. Though the fields lasted only a few years, the yields were extraordinary, up to a hundred-fold return on seed.

advances.name: Turkiskauppa
advances.text: Finland's vast forests teemed with fur-bearing animals, and the fur trade connected even the most remote Finnish settlements to the markets of Europe. The Finnish word 'raha', meaning money, originally meant 'fur pelt.'

advances.name: Frontier Resilience
advances.text: Life on the eastern frontier forged a unique Finnish character: the capacity to endure hardship, adapt to adversity, and fight tenaciously in defense of home and hearth.

advances.name: Savusauna
advances.text: The smoke sauna is the heart of Finnish community life. More than mere bathing, the sauna served as birthplace, healing house, and sacred space: the cleanest room in any Finnish settlement.

advances.name: Erämetsästäjät
advances.text: Finnish wilderness hunters roamed the vast interior forests, tracking game and guarding against intruders. Their intimate knowledge of the terrain made them invaluable as scouts and skirmishers.

advances.name: Finnish Church Tradition
advances.text: The Finnish church developed its own character within the wider Christian world, with parish churches serving as centers of both spiritual life and communal governance in the scattered Finnish settlements.

advances.name: Kauppakonttori
advances.text: Finnish trading posts connected the resources of the interior (furs, tar, timber) to the Hanseatic trade networks of the Baltic, bringing European goods and ideas to even the most remote Finnish towns.

advances.name: Castle-Building Tradition
advances.text: The great castles of Turku and Häme anchored Swedish-Finnish control over the region, serving as administrative centers and military strongholds that projected authority across the Finnish wilderness.

advances.name: Tervahauta
advances.text: Finnish tar kilns transformed the pine forests of Ostrobothnia into the naval stores that sealed the hulls of European fleets. By the 17th century, Finland produced over 80% of all Swedish tar exports.

advances.name: Tervakauppa
advances.text: The tar trade connected Finnish producers to the great shipbuilding centers of Europe. The Netherlands alone consumed three-quarters of Finnish tar output, and the trade brought unprecedented wealth to the coastal towns of Oulu and Kokkola.

advances.name: Mikael Agricola's Work
advances.text: Mikael Agricola, Bishop of Turku, created the written Finnish language and translated the New Testament into Finnish in 1548, laying the foundation for Finnish literacy and cultural identity.

event.title: The Father of Finnish Letters
event.text: Mikael Agricola, Bishop of Turku and student of Martin Luther himself, has completed his life's work: the translation of the New Testament into Finnish. For the first time, the Finnish language exists in written form. His Abckiria taught our people their letters, his Rucouskiria gave them prayers in their own tongue, and now Se Wsi Testamenti brings the word of God to every Finnish-speaking congregation. This is more than a religious achievement; it is the birth of Finnish literacy, the foundation upon which all future learning will be built. Agricola has given the Finnish people a voice that can endure across the centuries.

options.text: Let Agricola's work illuminate the minds of all Finns.

modifiers.name: Agricola's Legacy
modifiers.text: The work of Mikael Agricola lives on: a written Finnish language, a literate congregation, and a people who can read the word of God in their own tongue. This foundation of literacy and learning will serve Finland for centuries to come.

options.text: A written language forges a people's identity.

modifiers.name: Nation Building
modifiers.text: A written language is the foundation of a nation. Agricola's work creates a Finnish identity that transcends regional dialects and tribal boundaries, forging a people.

advances.name: Olavinlinna Tradition
advances.text: The fortress of Olavinlinna, St. Olaf's Castle, stands as the northernmost medieval stone fortress in the world, built to guard the contested frontier between Sweden-Finland and Novgorod.

advances.name: Rajapuolustus
advances.text: The organized defense of the Finnish border evolved from scattered manor garrisons into a systematic frontier defense, with disciplined troops trained to exploit the forests and waterways of the borderlands.

advances.name: Talvisoturi
advances.text: The harsh Finnish winters breed warriors unlike any in Europe. Winter soldiers move on skis through deep snow, fight in conditions that paralyze conventional armies, and use the frozen landscape itself as a weapon.

advances.name: Finnish Reformation
advances.text: The Reformation reached Finland through Mikael Agricola and other students of Luther. Unlike many European countries, Finland's Reformation was peaceful: a gradual transformation that brought literacy, education, and religious renewal.

advances.name: Talonpoikaisarmeija
advances.text: Finnish peasant warriors have fought in every conflict on the eastern frontier. Hardened by farming in the harshest conditions in Europe, they bring the same stubborn endurance to the battlefield.

advances.name: Ostrobothnian Trade Network
advances.text: The merchants of Ostrobothnia built a trade network that connected Finnish tar, timber, and furs to the markets of Europe, making the coastal towns of Oulu, Kokkola, and Vaasa prosperous trading centers.

advances.name: Sahalaitos
advances.text: The development of water-powered sawmills transformed Finland's timber industry. Sawn lumber could be exported in far greater quantities than raw logs, turning the endless Finnish forests into a source of industrial wealth.

advances.name: Merilinnoitus
advances.text: The great sea fortress guarding Helsinki harbor, built on a chain of islands at the entrance to the port, represents the apex of Finnish coastal defense, combining naval power with impregnable fortification.

advances.name: Recovery from the Great Wrath
advances.text: The catastrophic Russian occupation of 1714-1721 devastated Finland, whole provinces were depopulated, thousands deported to build St. Petersburg. The recovery took decades but forged a people of extraordinary resilience.

event.title: After the Great Wrath
event.text: The years of Russian occupation (the Isoviha, the Great Wrath) have finally ended. The toll has been catastrophic: thousands deported to build St. Petersburg, villages across Finland put to the torch, women and children taken as captives. In Ostrobothnia alone, half the population perished or fled. But Finland survives. The burned farmsteads can be rebuilt, the forests replanted, the population slowly recovered. The question is how we face this recovery. Do we harden ourselves against future invasion, building our military strength so that such devastation never occurs again? Or do we focus on rebuilding what was lost, restoring stability, growing our population, and healing the wounds of occupation?

options.text: Never again. We must be strong enough to resist any invader.

modifiers.name: Survivors of the Great Wrath
modifiers.text: The years of Russian occupation tested Finland to its limits, villages burned, populations deported, an entire generation scarred. But the Finnish people endured, and from the ashes of the Great Wrath emerged a nation hardened by suffering and determined to rebuild.

options.text: We shall never be conquered so easily again.

modifiers.name: National Resolve
modifiers.text: The trauma of the Great Wrath has hardened Finland's resolve. The people who endured occupation, deportation, and devastation emerge with a determination that no future invader shall find them unprepared.

advances.name: Frontier Administration Reform
advances.text: The modernization of Finnish frontier administration brought effective governance to even the most remote districts, replacing ad hoc border defense with systematic provincial management.

advances.name: Puutavaravienti
advances.text: Finnish lumber exports grew dramatically in the 18th century as the sawmill industry expanded. Processed timber, naval stores, and tar flowed from Finnish ports to the shipyards and construction sites of Europe.

advances.name: Jääkärit
advances.text: Finnish Jaegers, light infantry specialists trained in independent skirmish tactics, expert marksmen who fight in small units across difficult terrain. Their mastery of forest warfare makes them elite troops.

advances.name: Finnish National Awakening
advances.text: The compilation of the Kalevala from ancient oral poetry, the rise of Finnish-language literature, and the spread of national consciousness through newspapers and education transformed Finnish identity from a regional dialect into a national culture.

event.title: The Finnish National Awakening
event.text: A new spirit stirs across Finland. Scholars, poets, and patriots have begun to articulate what it means to be Finnish, not as subjects of a greater power, but as a people with their own language, their own traditions, their own destiny. The Kalevala, compiled from ancient oral poetry, has given the Finnish people an epic to rival Homer. The Finnish language, once dismissed as a peasant tongue, is finding its voice in literature, science, and governance. Newspapers in Finnish spread ideas of national consciousness to every corner of the land. This awakening is not born of revolution but of culture: the quiet conviction that a people who share a language, a landscape, and a history deserve to shape their own future.

advances.name: Ruukki
advances.text: Finnish ironworks, ruukit, combined the country's rich iron ore deposits with abundant charcoal from the forests to produce high-quality iron. These early industrial establishments laid the groundwork for Finnish manufacturing.

advances.name: Sisu
advances.text: Sisu: the Finnish concept of extraordinary determination, courage, and resilience in the face of overwhelming adversity. It is not mere stubbornness but a profound national character forged by centuries of frontier hardship.

destiny.name: Finnish Destiny
destiny.text: Finland has risen as a sovereign nation. The path ahead will be shaped by the choices we make, whether we forge an impregnable northern fortress or a prosperous Baltic trading power.

event.title: The Finnish Destiny
event.text: Finland stands united and stable: a nation of forests, lakes, and iron determination. The question of what we shall become is no longer abstract. Our choices will shape the north for centuries.

options.text: Our destiny is in our hands.

destiny.name: The Karelian March
destiny.text: Secure the ancient fortress of Korela and Sortavala on the Ladoga shore, the county the Peace of Stolbovo gave to the Finnish crown, and establish Finnish control over the Karelian borderlands.

conditions.text: Chose Land of a Thousand Lakes

event.title: The Karelian March
event.text: The fortress of Korela has fallen under Finnish control. For centuries this ancient stronghold guarded the border between East and West, now it guards Finland. Our soldiers patrol the Karelian forests, and the eastern frontier is ours to defend. The march into Karelia has begun.

destiny.name: Shield of the North
destiny.text: Push deeper into Karelia, securing Olonets and Pryazha in the Aunus lands, and build Viborg, the castle town of the eastern border, up into a bulwark.

conditions.text: We own Viborg and its development is at least 22

event.title: Shield of the North
event.text: Finnish arms have pushed deep into Karelia. The lands of Aunus, once beyond our reach, now fly the Finnish banner. Our soldiers patrol a frontier that stretches from the frozen north to the shores of Lake Ladoga, and behind it Viborg has been built up into the bulwark of the border. The question now is how we consolidate these gains. Do we fortify every pass and ford, turning Karelia into an impenetrable defensive zone? Or do we focus on integrating the Karelian peoples, making them Finnish in heart as well as in law?

options.text: Fortify every approach. Let no army pass.

modifiers.name: Fortified Frontier
modifiers.text: Every pass, ford, and forest trail in Karelia has been mapped, fortified, and garrisoned. The eastern frontier is an impenetrable defensive zone, though the focus on military preparation has drawn resources from commerce.

options.text: These Karelians are our kin. Let them be Finns.

modifiers.name: Karelian Integration
modifiers.text: The Karelian peoples are being welcomed as fellow Finns, shared language, shared faith, shared destiny. Finnish administrators bring order and opportunity to the new provinces.

destiny.name: Unconquerable Finland
destiny.text: Control the Neva River and the fortresses of Narva and Koporye, and raise Helsinge into a fortress harbour twice the place it was, sealing Finland's dominance over the eastern Baltic approaches. No army shall pass through Finnish lands without our leave.

conditions.text: We own Helsinge and its development is at least 26

event.title: Unconquerable Finland
event.text: The Neva River and the fortress of Narva are in Finnish hands, and a sea fortress guards the grown harbour of Helsinge. No power can approach Finland from the east without passing through territory we command, and no Baltic fleet can operate without Finnish acquiescence. Finland has achieved what few believed possible: a northern nation, born of forests and lakes, now stands as an impregnable power that no invader can subdue. How shall we wield this strength? Through the perfection of winter warfare, making our armies the most feared in the north? Or through the quiet authority of a nation that cannot be conquered, projecting power through the sheer impossibility of our defeat?

options.text: Our winters shall be our weapon.

modifiers.name: Winter Warfare Doctrine
modifiers.text: Finnish armies have perfected the art of winter warfare, rapid reinforcement through frozen terrain, relentless endurance in conditions that break other armies, and a fighting spirit forged in the harshest winters in Europe. Naval readiness suffers as resources flow to the land forces.

options.text: Let the world know: Finland cannot be broken.

modifiers.name: Invincible Frontier
modifiers.text: Finland's reputation as an unconquerable nation projects power without a sword being drawn. The crown's authority is strengthened by national pride, and Finland's diplomatic position grows ever stronger.

destiny.name: Ostrobothnian Wealth
destiny.text: Establish tar as the foundation of Finnish commerce. Fill the treasury through the export of Finland's forest wealth to the markets of Europe.

children.text: Tar is produced in the market
Tar is traded in the market

event.title: Ostrobothnian Wealth
event.text: Finnish tar flows through the markets of Europe. From the kilns of Ostrobothnia to the shipyards of Amsterdam and London, our forest wealth has become indispensable. The treasury swells with the profits of this trade, and Finnish merchants speak with growing authority in the counting houses of the Baltic.

destiny.name: Baltic Tar Kings
destiny.text: Make Uleåborg the tar harbour of the north and dominate the northern Baltic tar trade. Burn tar in kilns in four places of the realm, as the peasants of Ostrobothnia did, and fill the treasury to finance the expansion of Finnish commercial networks.

conditions.text: We own Uleåborg and its development is at least 18
Has a Tar Kiln or a Tervanpolttaja tar kiln in at least 4 locations

event.title: Baltic Tar Kings
event.text: Uleåborg has grown into the tar harbour of the north, and with it we hold the heart of the northern tar trade. Finnish bankers finance the expansion of our commercial networks, and no ship sails the Baltic without Finnish tar in its hull. We have become the tar kings of the north. The question is how to build on this dominance. Shall we expand our trade fleet, projecting Finnish commercial power across the seas? Or shall we invest in developing the Finnish interior, turning raw wealth into lasting prosperity?

options.text: Build ships. Let the Finnish flag fly in every port.

modifiers.name: Finnish Trade Fleet
modifiers.text: A growing fleet of Finnish merchantmen carries tar, timber, and furs to every port in the Baltic. Sailors flock to the coastal towns, though the cavalry traditions of the interior have been neglected.

options.text: Invest in our land. True wealth grows from within.

modifiers.name: Interior Development
modifiers.text: Investment flows into the Finnish interior, new roads, reformed administration, and banking institutions that channel commercial wealth into lasting development. Rapid growth brings some inflationary pressure.

destiny.name: Northern Commercial Empire
destiny.text: Take Tallinn and command the Baltic trade routes, and build Åbo into the mercantile heart of the northern seas: twice the town it was, with a merchants' quarter of its own.

conditions.text: Åbo is owned and has a Merchants Quarters, Grand Marketplace or Commerce Center
We own Åbo and its development is at least 27

event.title: Northern Commercial Empire
event.text: Tallinn has fallen into Finnish hands, and with it command of the Baltic trade routes. Finnish merchants dominate the commerce of the north: tar, timber, furs, and iron flow through our markets to every corner of Europe. From a frontier at the edge of civilization, Finland has become the mercantile heart of the northern seas, and Åbo is twice the town it was. Shall we use this power to build diplomatic influence, making Finland the indispensable partner of every trading nation? Or shall we turn inward, using our commercial wealth to pioneer industrial development and modernize our nation?

options.text: Finland shall be the merchant of the north.

modifiers.name: Mercantile Dominion
modifiers.text: Finland's commercial network spans the Baltic and beyond. Finnish merchants are welcome in every port, Finnish intelligence networks map every market, and Finnish ships enforce favorable trading conditions.

options.text: Commerce funds the future. Invest in industry.

modifiers.name: Industrial Pioneer
modifiers.text: Commercial wealth funds a program of modernization and industrialization. Finland's diverse peoples are united by prosperity, and the legitimacy of Finnish rule grows with every new enterprise.

units.name: Rajasotilaat
units.text: Finnish border soldiers, hardy frontier infantry trained to defend the eastern borderlands through ambush, fortification, and stubborn resistance in the forests and marshes.

units.name: Erämetsästäjät
units.text: Finnish wilderness hunters, woodsmen-scouts who know every trail, lake, and hiding place in the vast interior forests. They move fast, strike first from concealment, and vanish into the trees sooner than stand against a charge.

units.name: Rajapuolustajat
units.text: Finnish border defenders, organized frontier garrison troops who combine pike discipline with the defensive instincts bred by generations of border warfare.

units.name: Talvisoturit
units.text: Elite Finnish winter warriors, infantry adapted to fight in the harshest conditions, exploiting snow, ice, and frozen terrain to neutralize numerical superiority.

units.name: Talonpoikaissoturit
units.text: Finnish peasant warriors, farmers who take up arms when the frontier is threatened, bringing the same unyielding endurance to battle that sustains them through the northern winters.

units.name: Jääkärit
units.text: Finnish Jaegers, elite light infantry trained in independent skirmish tactics. Expert marksmen fighting in small detachments, they excel in forest warfare and irregular combat.

buildings.name: Rajakartano
buildings.text: Fortified border manors serving as military outposts and administrative centers along the Finnish frontier, their garrisons providing the first line of defense against eastern raiders.

buildings.name: Savusauna
buildings.text: The smoke sauna is the heart of Finnish community life. More than mere bathing, the sauna served as birthplace, healing house, and sacred space: the cleanest room in any Finnish settlement.

buildings.text: Finnish tar kilns transformed the pine forests of Ostrobothnia into the naval stores that sealed the hulls of European fleets. By the 17th century, Finland produced over 80% of all Swedish tar exports.

buildings.text: The development of water-powered sawmills transformed Finland's timber industry. Sawn lumber could be exported in far greater quantities than raw logs, turning the endless Finnish forests into a source of industrial wealth.

buildings.text: The great sea fortress guarding Helsinki harbor, built on a chain of islands at the entrance to the port, represents the apex of Finnish coastal defense, combining naval power with impregnable fortification.

buildings.name: Ruukki
buildings.text: Finnish ironworks, ruukit, combined the country's rich iron ore deposits with abundant charcoal from the forests to produce high-quality iron. These early industrial establishments laid the groundwork for Finnish manufacturing.

buildings.name: Talvitukikohta
buildings.text: A fortified winter warfare base designed to sustain military operations deep in the Finnish interior. Thick log walls, heated barracks, and concealed supply depots allow Finnish armies to operate in conditions that paralyze any invader.

buildings.name: Pohjolan Kauppahalli
buildings.text: A grand northern trading hall where Finnish merchants conduct business with traders from across Europe. Warehouses for tar and timber, counting rooms for bankers, and halls where commercial agreements shape the economy of the Baltic.

list.name: Häradshövding Ting
list.text: The medieval Swedish-Finnish hundred court, where the district judge (häradshövding) presided over an assize court alongside twelve farmer lay judges from the surrounding hundred. The 1634 constitution counted Finland among the realm's lagsagor; in practice the institution was older still, with rural disputes settled at seasonal ting where at least seven lay judges had to be present for jurisdiction. The ting was the working bedrock of Finnish self-rule under Swedish law.

list.name: Bishopric of Åbo
list.text: The Diocese of Turku (Åbo), first mentioned in 1259, covered all of medieval Finland and answered to the archiepiscopal see of Uppsala. Until the late thirteenth century the bishop was de facto secular leader of Finland; afterward the cathedral chapter at Åbo, the Dominican convent founded 1249, and a parish network that doubled as local administration kept the church the realm's central institution. The first native Finnish bishop was named in 1291; thereafter every incumbent was Finnish-born.

list.name: Rusthåll
list.text: The cavalry farms of Finland. A farmstead wealthy enough to keep a horse and an armed rider for the crown was freed of its land tax in return, and its master answered for man, mount and gear at the yearly muster. The bargain was older than the regiments it filled, and the allotment system of Charles XI fixed it in the 1680s as the rusthåll, which the Finns called rustholli. The riders became famous. The farms that mounted them were an office of the crown: a register, an inspection and a tax ledger.

list.name: Birkarl Lapp Tribute
list.text: The pirkkalaiset, royally-licensed merchants of the Tornio, Luleå, and Piteå valleys who from the thirteenth to seventeenth centuries held monopoly rights over commerce with and tax extraction from the Sami of Lappmarken. Each river valley constituted a separate lappmark with its own birkarls; the crown received its share, the birkarls grew rich, and the Sami were locked into a colonial relationship that ended only when the three river towns received their 1621 town charters and the state took over directly.
